examples.solution_text:
(a) The two path lengths are
$\begin{aligned}L_{AC}&=6+7=13\text{ days}\\L_{ABDE}&=6+5+2+3=16\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
The minimum completion time is $16$ days, with critical path $A$–$B$–$D$–$E$. Reducing $C$ makes $A$–$C$ take $11$ days, but the critical path still takes $16$ days. No time is saved.

(b) With $A=4$ days,
$\begin{aligned}L_{AC}&=4+7=11\text{ days}\\L_{ABDE}&=4+5+2+3=14\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
The project takes $14$ days. The critical path remains $A$–$B$–$D$–$E$. Both paths contain $A$, so both shorten by $2$ days.

(c) With $B=2$ days and $E=1$ day,
$\begin{aligned}L_{AC}&=6+7=13\text{ days}\\L_{ABDE}&=6+2+2+1=11\text{ days}\\\text{Time saved}&=16-13=3\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
The new critical path is $A$–$C$, and the project takes $13$ days. The activity reductions total $5$ days, but the unchanged path prevents a saving greater than $3$ days.

(d) The longest path unaffected by reducing $B$ is $A$–$C$, at $13$ days.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Greatest useful reduction}&=16-13=3\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
Reducing $B$ to $2$ days makes both paths critical at $13$ days. Further reduction in $B$ alone saves no additional time.

The original path lengths are
$\begin{aligned}L_{ACEG}&=3+8+5+3=19\text{ days}\\L_{ACFH}&=3+8+4+5=20\text{ days}\\L_{BDEG}&=5+4+5+3=17\text{ days}\\L_{BDFH}&=5+4+4+5=18\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$

(a) Both paths through $C$ shorten when $C$ is reduced. The longest path avoiding $C$ is $B$–$D$–$F$–$H$, at $18$ days.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Greatest useful reduction}&=20-18=2\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
With $C=6$ days, the four paths take $17$, $18$, $17$ and $18$ days. The two paths through $F$–$H$ are now critical; further reduction in $C$ alone does not shorten both.

(b) The path $B$–$D$–$E$–$G$ contains none of the activities that can be shortened. Its $17$ days give a lower bound for the project.

Reduce $F$ by $1$ day, to $3$ days. The four path lengths become $19$, $19$, $17$ and $17$ days. The two critical paths both contain $C$.

Reduce $C$ by $2$ days, to $6$ days. The four path lengths become $17$, $17$, $17$ and $17$ days. The project now takes $17$ days, saving $3$ days.

To reach $17$ days, $A$–$C$–$E$–$G$ requires at least $2$ days of reduction in $C$. Also, $B$–$D$–$F$–$H$ requires at least $1$ day of reduction in $F$ or $H$. Reducing $F$ costs less than reducing $H$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Least cost}&=2\times500+1\times300\\&=\$1300.\end{aligned}$
The least-cost plan reduces $C$ by $2$ days and $F$ by $1$ day.

The original path lengths are
$\begin{aligned}L_{ACF}&=10+7+8=25\text{ days}\\L_{BDF}&=4+6+8=18\text{ days}\\L_{BEG}&=4+3+7=14\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
The critical path is $A$–$C$–$F$.

(a) The unchanged $18$-day path $B$–$D$–$F$ limits the useful saving to $25-18=7$ days. Both available reductions shorten only $A$–$C$–$F$, so use the cheaper days of $A$ first.

Reduce $A$ by $5$ days and $C$ by $2$ days. These reductions respect both limits. The three paths then take $18$, $18$ and $14$ days.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Least cost}&=5\times120+2\times180\\&=600+360\\&=\$960.\end{aligned}$
The project takes $18$ days and saves $7$ days.

(b) The maximum available reduction on $A$–$C$–$F$ is
$\begin{aligned}\text{Maximum reduction}&=3+2+2=7\text{ days}\\\text{Lowest possible project time}&\geq25-7=18\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
Reduce $A$ to $7$ days, $C$ to $5$ days and $F$ to $6$ days. Leave $E$ unchanged.
$\begin{aligned}L_{ACF}&=7+5+6=18\text{ days}\\L_{BDF}&=4+6+6=16\text{ days}\\L_{BEG}&=4+3+7=14\text{ days}.\end{aligned}$
This achieves the lower bound, so the greatest saving is $7$ days. Every available day of reduction in $A$, $C$ and $F$ is required to reach it. Reducing $E$ adds cost without shortening the project.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Least cost}&=3\times120+2\times180+2\times100\\&=360+360+200\\&=\$920.\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: The diagram gives exactly two paths: AC = 6+7 = 13 and ABDE = 6+5+2+3 = 16 days. (a) Reducing C to 5 leaves the longest path at 16 days, saving zero. (b) Reducing A to 4 gives path lengths 11 and 14 days; ABDE remains critical. (c) Reducing B to 2 and E to 1 gives path lengths 13 and 11 days; AC becomes critical and saves 16−13 = 3 days. (d) A reduction x in B gives project duration max(13,16−x), so the greatest useful reduction is 3 days. At B = 2 both paths take 13 days.

The diagram gives four paths: ACEG = 3+8+5+3 = 19 days; ACFH = 3+8+4+5 = 20 days; BDEG = 5+4+5+3 = 17 days; BDFH = 5+4+4+5 = 18 days. (a) Reducing C by x gives lengths 19−x, 20−x, 17 and 18. The greatest useful reduction is therefore 2 days. (b) Unchangeable BDEG establishes a 17-day lower bound. Reaching it requires at least 2 days off C and at least 1 day off F or H. These reductions also satisfy ACFH's required 3-day reduction. F is cheaper than H, so reducing C by 2 days and F by 1 day achieves four 17-day paths at the minimum cost, 2×500+300 = $1300.

The paths ACF, BDF and BEG take 25,18,14 days. (a) BDF is unchanged, so the greatest saving is 7 days. Minimising 120a+180c subject to a+c≥7, a≤5 and c≤4 gives a=5,c=2. The paths become 18,18,14 and the cost is $960. (b) ACF can shorten by at most 3+2+2 = 7 days, establishing an 18-day lower bound. Taking all allowed reductions in A,C,F gives paths 18,16,14 and achieves that bound. Each of those reductions is necessary; E is unnecessary. The saving is 7 days and the least cost is 3×120+2×180+2×100 = $920.
